item.title: Blue Jays Surge in Second Half to End Dodge City’s Season
item.description: The postseason run for the Dodge City Red Demons came to a close Wednesday night as Junction City used a big second-half push to defeat Dodge City 70–56 in Junction City.

item.title: Beyond Reason
item.description: The family went skiing this weekend. What struck me immediately is that skiing is a completely different workout than anything we get in the city. It demands flexibility, raw strength, balance, endurance. There are moments that test your pain tolerance. It engages every muscle group — the large stabilizers, the core, even the tiny neglected lower-back muscles I don’t remember ever existing. And that’s just getting the foot into the ski boot.

item.title: City approves bid for 2026 street reconstruction project
item.description: The Dodge City Commission approved the bid for the 2026 Street Reconstruction project at its regular meeting on Monday.

item.title: Clocks “Spring” Forward This Sunday
item.description: Daylight saving time ends this Sunday. Before heading to bed Saturday, March 7, clocks should be moved forward an hour (most electronics will automatically update the time). Time change will officially happen on Sunday, March 8, at 2 a.m., when time will move forward to 3 a.m.

item.title: Kansans on food assistance can’t buy candy, soda beginning in February 2027
item.description: TOPEKA — Kansans receiving food assistance can’t buy soda or candy with those dollars beginning in 2027, Gov. Laura Kelly said Wednesday.

item.title: Early prenatal care declines across US, reversing years of progress
item.description: Nearly a quarter of pregnant women aren’t getting prenatal care in the early stages of pregnancy, according to a new analysis from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

item.title: Celebrating FFA Week
item.description: Every year since 1948, FFA members, agriculture teachers, alumni and supporters have come together to celebrate National FFA Week. The tradition is held during the week of Feb. 22, in honor of George Washington’s birthday — a fitting tribute to a leader who valued agriculture and innovation.
